item.title: Mean Girls The Musical — Sat Nov 7, 7:30 PM — Davis Musical Theatre Co. (DMTC)
item.description:
November 6 through November 29, 2026 Cady Heron may have grown up on an African savanna, but nothing prepared her for the wild and vicious ways of her strange new home: suburban Illinois. How will this naïve newbie rise to the top of the popularity pecking order? By taking on The Plastics, a trio of lionized frenemies led by the charming but ruthless Regina George. But when Cady and her friends devise a “Revenge Party” to end Regina’s reign, she learns the hard way that you can’t cross a queen bee without getting stung. Recommended for ages 13 and up
Source: The Dirt

item.description:

item.description:

We'll be there to give them the information they need to get their ballots cured and their votes counted! item.title: DHS Ski Swap — Sun Nov 8, 9:00 AM — Davis Senior High School South Gym
item.description:
Looking for affordable ski and snowboard gear for the upcoming season? Come shop the Davis High School Blue Devil Ski Team Ski Swap, featuring a wide selection of new and gently used ski and snowboard equipment, outerwear, and winter sports apparel. Whether you’re a beginner gearing up for your first season or an experienced skier looking for a bargain, you’ll find great deals on quality equipment and clothing. Proceeds from the event support the Davis High School Ski Team. Admission is $5 per person, and children 10 and under are free. Have gear to sell or donate? Community members can consign used ski and snowboard equipment and clothing or make donations to support the sale. Consignment and donation drop-off times are Saturday, 11/7 from 4:00 to 8:00 p.m. and on Sunday. 11/8 from 7:30 to 8:30 a.m.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Art Cafe — Sun Nov 8, 10:00 AM — Davis Arts Center
item.description:

Create at your own pace using provided materials, or bring your own (no hazardous or materials with strong orders). Adults and Teens only. AGES 13+ Price: FREE 2nd & 4th Sundays, 10 am-12 pm Fall dates: 9/13, 9/27 10/11, 10/25 11/8, 11/22 12/13 No pre-registration required. Just drop in! Price: FREE

item.title: Backyard Book Swap — Sun Nov 8, 10:00 AM — 1118 L Street
item.description:
Backyard Book Swap with Yolo County Caregivers Collective 2nd Sunday of every month, 10am – 12pm 1118 L Street, Davis
Ready for a new read? Join our monthly book swap! This free playgroup meets on the second Sunday of every month. Bring a gently-loved book or two to swap, discover your mini’s next favorite read, and connect with other bookworms. Our book swap is a great way to refresh your bookshelf, make new friends, and add an exciting new chapter to your social life! We’ll have bubbles, simple arts, and space to play for the little ones. Each month features a different theme and free refreshments will be provided too. Together we can build community around the joy of reading.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: The Amazing Bubble Man Live — Sun Nov 8, 11:30 AM — Davis Veterans Memorial Theatre
item.description:
Louis Pearl has been thrilling audiences around the world for over 30 years with the art, magic, science and fun of bubbles. Louis Pearl has been thrilling audiences around the world for over 30 years with the art, magic, science and fun of bubbles. He is a favorite at the Edinburgh Fringe Festival, where he has enjoyed 14 years of sell-out success. Louis explores the breath-taking dynamics of bubbles, combining comedy and artistry with audience participation and enough spellbinding bubble tricks to keep everyone mesmerized. From square bubbles, bubbles inside bubbles, fog-filled bubbles, giant bubbles, bubble volcanoes, tornados and trampolines to people inside bubbles, the Amazing Bubble Man conjures shrieks of laughter and gasps of amazement from all ages. Most shows will also feature multi instrumentalist Jet Black Pearl accompanying Louis with bubbly music to double your pleasure. Home

item.title: Above Bone — Sun Nov 8, 12:00 PM — Axis Gallery
item.description: ADERO WILLARD ABOVE BONE November 6–29, 2026 Reception and Artist Talk on Saturday, November 7, 5–8 PM Artist in the gallery on Sundays, November 8 and 29, 12–5 PM Axis Gallery presents Above Bone, an exhibition of ceramic sculpture by Sacramento artist Adero Willard, on view November 6 through 29, 2026. The exhibition brings together new work and pieces never before shown in Sacramento or on the West Coast. Join the artist for the reception and artist talk on Saturday, November 7, 5–8 PM. ABOUT THE EXHIBITION Above Bone refers to what is beneath, the layers, and what emerges. Clay sculptural vessels of heads and body forms explore death, regeneration, new growth, and what is hidden. Adero wrestles clay into expressive forms and creates surfaces dense in color and pattern: thick clay and delicately etched vines and flowers. The forms are camouflaged, as if growing from or being returned to the ground. Layered colorful patterns, resists, and luster build up over multiple firings. Pat

item.title: Capturing Memories of Grief/Capturando Memorias del Duelo — Sun Nov 8, 12:00 PM — Axis Gallery
item.description: SUMMER VENTIS AND LINA RINCÓN CAPTURING MEMORIES OF GRIEF/CAPTURANDO MEMORIAS DEL DUELO November 6–29, 2026 Reception on Saturday, November 7, 5–8 PM The project, “Capturing Memories of Grief,” is a collaboration between artist Summer Ventis, sociologist and poet Lina Rincón, and you. Together, we explore the intersection of grief, memory, and image. We began this project with a conversation about our shared experience of losing a parent. When we recalled these experiences, we learned that we both had memories that centered around images, photographs, and the process of photography as a way to make sense of and process the meanings of our loss. In Fall of 2025, we began a series of grief-themed tours of works in the Crocker Art Museum’s collection. At the end of the tours, participants gathered to share and document our memories of grief and loss and how they connect with different types of images. We invited participants to consider grief and loss broadly; while we first connected

item.title: Second Sunday Bingo — Sun Nov 8, 12:00 PM — Davis Odd Fellows
item.description:
Odd Fellows Bingo (LH)
When: Second Sunday of the month Where: 415 2nd St, Davis, CA 95616, USA (map)
Description: Second Sunday Bingo at the Lodge. Doors open at noon and Bingo begins at 1 p.m. Open to all adults. Davis Odd Fellows Bingo! is a wonderful way for the community to support the many needy non-profit organizations here in Davis. Each month, Davis Odd Fellows Bingo! connects with a local organization that needs assistance. Community members, friends, and family are encouraged and welcomed to come to the Davis Odd Fellows Lodge for an afternoon of to fun playing Davis Bingo. For as little as $12, you can sit with friends and chat or meet new people while helping people in our community.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Art in Action: Wonderful Wire Tree Sculptures — Sun Nov 8, 1:00 PM — Pence Gallery
item.description: Art in Action: Wonderful Wire Tree Sculptures Sunday, November 8, 1-3 PM $5 Members, $10 Non-Members (per person, all materials included) Transform wire and other materials into a beautiful tree! Drawing inspiration from Danilo Campos’ landscapes of our region, fashion a wire tree sculpture that is mounted on rocks and wood using wire, beads, paper, felt, and fringe. How it works: Art in Action engages kids in art projects that are fun, creative, and collaborative with their family members. This is a drop-in program for ages 5-12. No registration in advance is required, but space and supplies are limited to the first 25 participants and are available on a first come, first served basis. When you arrive, pay with cash or card at the front desk. A parent or adult caregiver is required to stay, but only has to pay for the project for themselves if they are also doing art. Stay as long or as short as you like over the two hour period. We have a different Art in Action family workshop eve

item.title: Arcis Saxophone Quartet: JSB:48 — Sun Nov 8, 2:00 PM — Vanderhoef Studio Theatre
item.description:
Munich’s Arcis Saxophone Quartet presents JSB:48 in the Mondavi Center’s Vanderhoef Studio Theatre. Bach’s fugues meet newly commissioned preludes by Aleksey Igudesman, Huey Ching Chong, Theresa Zaremba and Nyokabi Kariuki, alongside music by Kapustin and Shostakovich and connections to Radiohead, Brad Mehldau and Bernstein. Sunday, November 8, 2026, at 2:00 p.m. Pacific time. A second performance takes place at 7:30 p.m. Approximate running time: 90 minutes, including intermission. The programme uses amplification, with recorded accompaniment in selected works. Tickets and current prices: https://www.mondaviarts.org/whats-on/arcis-saxophone-quartet
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Artist Talk with Gioia Fonda — Sun Nov 8, 2:00 PM — Pence Gallery
item.description:
Artist Talk with Gioia Fonda Sunday, November 8, 2-3:30 PM (Free) Gioia Fonda is a multi-media artist and educator whose new series harkens back to her still-life work from almost 30 years ago. Enjoy a lively talk with Fonda that sets the stage for exploration into her interest in the relationships between objects, the influence of mentors such as Charlie Gill, and more. Visitors can view portraits of things: Paintings by Gioia Fonda and Charlie Gill on display at the Pence Gallery from October 9 – November 29, 2026.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Pianist Michelle Cann and Flutist Ráyo Furuta in Concert — Sun Nov 8, 5:00 PM — Ann E. Pitzer Center
item.description:
Collaborators and star performers of their instruments — Grammy Award-winning pianist Michelle Cann and Mexican Japanese American flutist Ráyo Furuta — will give an unforgettable performance at the Ann E. Pitzer Center at UC Davis. The concert is Sunday, Nov. 8 at 5 p.m. Their collaborative program includes performances of Florence Price’s 2 Fantasies for Flute and Piano, Sergei Rachmaninoff’s Sonata for Piano and Flute and Yuko Uebayashi’s “Souvenis de Pervenche.” $10 UC Davis students; $14 children (under 18), $21.60 faculty/staff and $24 Adult.

item.title: Davis Odd Fellows Classic Film Fest — Sun Nov 8, 7:00 PM — Davis Odd Fellows
item.description: Davis Odd Fellows Classic Film Fest returns to the Davis Odd Fellows Hall for a three-week run starting Sunday, November 1st. The genre for this series of films is Screwball Comedies of the 1960s & 1970s. Everyone is welcome to enjoy these films. Doors open at 6:29 p.m. and the films start at 7:01 p.m.Popcorn is provided free of charge. The bar will be open to purchase beer, wine, or soft drinks. Davis Enterprise Film Critic/Reviewer Derrick Bang will give a short talk before each movie about interesting details on the plot, director, actors, and fun things to look for while watching. He’ll do a quick Q&A afterwards. According to Bazooka will play before each movie. November 1st we kick off with “One, Two, Three” a 1961 American political comedy film directed by Billy Wilder and written by Wilder and I. A. L. Diamond. This film stars James Cagney, Horst Buchholz, and Arlene Francis. November 8th we bring you Mel Brooks’1968 comedy, “The Producers” starring Zero Mostel and Gene Wild

item.title: Manetti Shrem Museum: Together Again, 1960–2026, Perspectives from UC Davis’ Fine Arts Collection — Sat Nov 21, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description: Together Again inaugurates the Manetti Shrem Museum’s ongoing collection galleries. This exhibition highlighting the collection will be on long-term view, accompanied by temporary exhibitions each fall and winter. The ongoing collection galleries trace a history of art forged from UC Davis and throughout Northern California. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, this presentation proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri. item.title: Manetti Shrem Museum: Together Again, 1960–2026, Perspectives from UC Davis’ Fine Arts Collection — Thu Nov 19, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description: Together Again inaugurates the Manetti Shrem Museum’s ongoing collection galleries. This exhibition highlighting the collection will be on long-term view, accompanied by temporary exhibitions each fall and winter. The ongoing collection galleries trace a history of art forged from UC Davis and throughout Northern California. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, this presentation proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri. Together Again builds bridges between who we were and who we are becoming at UC Davis, and affirms the Manetti Shrem Museum as home to the complex story of No
